name: array
title: Array
tagline: Discrete objects in rows×cols groups; derives the total, repeated-addition sentence, commutativity, factors and fraction of a set; a KS1/2 manipulative.
description: A set of discrete countable objects (dots, unit tiles, counters or stars) arranged into rows equal groups of cols — drawn either as a tight rows × cols array or as separated, ringed clusters of objects. The total, the rows × cols product, the repeated-addition sentence (cols + cols + … = total), the commuted reading, the fraction of the set when groups are selected (k/rows), the of-amount value (k × cols), the one-part division (total ÷ rows) and the factor / prime verdict are all computed from the two factors — you never author a count or a result. Equal groups, repeated addition, times-table arrays, commutativity, factors versus primes, and fraction of a set are all one figure: a primary (KS1/KS2) manipulative with chunky tactile objects, a categorical colour per group, and a fill-in stem sentence. Readouts and factors occlude to "?" for questions; counting the objects is always the method. Distinct from the area model, which is a measured rectangle rather than countable objects.
whenToUse: Reach for this for the discrete multiplicative structure of primary number: an array of objects for a times table, equal groups with rings for "lots of" / repeated addition, a fraction of a set, or a factor rectangle. Author the two factors: rows is the number of equal groups (and, for a fraction of a set, the fraction's denominator); cols is the number of objects in each group. Everything else is derived. Choose layout: "array" draws a tight rows × cols grid (the array picture — best for times tables, commutativity and factor rectangles); layout: "groups" draws rows separated clusters, each ringed, of cols objects each (the equal-groups / repeated-addition picture). Common configurations: count it — show: { total: true } with occlude: ["total"] for a "how many?" answer space (the objects stay, only the number is "?"); times table — show: { product: true, addition: true } to pair 3 × 4 = 12 with 4 + 4 + 4 = 12; commutativity — show: { commute: true } appends 4 × 3 to the same picture, and a second block draws the partner orientation; equal groups — layout: "groups", rings: true, show: { addition: true, product: true } ("4 groups of 3"); fraction of a set — set rows to the denominator, cols to total ÷ denominator, select to the numerator k (the first k groups go amber), labelEachGroup: true to tag each group "1/denominator", and show: { fraction: true, ofAmount: true, division: true } for ¾ of 20 = 15 worked through 20 ÷ 4 = 5; factors / primes — show: { factors: true } states "12 = 3 × 4" for a rectangle, or "7 is prime (only 1 × 7)" for a 1-wide strip; missing factor — occlude: ["rows"] or ["cols"] hides one factor everywhere it appears ("? × 4 = 12"); the stem sentence "__ groups of __ is __" rides along when stem: true and blanks the occluded value. Keep rows, cols, object and layout steady across one lesson so pupils track one picture; build richer flows by sequencing blocks (staged build → worked → question), never by combining a staged steps array with anything else. Staged builds come in two shapes: construct it — start with reveal: 0 (an empty frame of ghost groups), step reveal up one group at a time, then turn the readouts on at the end; or work the calculation — start with the full figure and no readouts, then reveal the product, the repeated addition and the stem over the stages. Synonyms teachers use: array, arrays, rows and columns, equal groups, groups of, lots of, repeated addition, times tables, multiplication, commutative, commutativity, factors, factor pairs, prime, composite, fraction of a set, fraction of an amount, fraction of a quantity, sharing into equal groups.

rows.description: The number of equal GROUPS (drawn top to bottom). In a tight array these are the rows; in "groups" layout these are the separate clusters. For a fraction of a set this is the fraction's DENOMINATOR (the set is split into `rows` equal groups). The first factor of the product rows × cols.

cols.description: The number of objects IN EACH group (drawn left to right in a tight array; arranged compactly inside each cluster in "groups" layout). The second factor of the product, and the size of one equal part (total ÷ rows).

layout.description: How the groups are drawn. "array" (default): a tight rows × cols grid of objects — the array picture, for times tables, commutativity and factor rectangles. "groups": rows separated clusters, each holding cols objects arranged compactly — the equal-groups / repeated-addition picture. Same maths either way (total = rows × cols); pick the picture the lesson wants.

object.description: The countable glyph. "dot" (default) a filled disc; "tile" a rounded unit square (the unit-squares picture); "counter" a two-ring disc; "star" and "heart" friendlier shapes for younger pupils. Purely how each object looks — every object is one unit regardless.

colorByGroup.description: Give each group its own colour from the categorical palette (blue, teal, purple, coral, green, cycling). Helps pupils SEE the groups as distinct — the default in "groups" layout, off (single blue) in "array" layout. Amber is never used here; it is reserved for the selected part / result. Selected groups are amber regardless of this flag.

rings.description: Draw a soft rounded loop around each group — the "equal groups" scaffolding. Default true in "groups" layout, false in "array" layout (set true to ring each ROW of a tight array, bridging array ↔ equal groups). Rings are construction-grey, not amber.

select.description: How many groups are CHOSEN — the first `select` groups go amber (the fraction numerator). With select = k the model derives the fraction k/rows of the set, the of-amount value k × cols and shows them by default. select 0 (default) chooses nothing. Clamped to rows. Use for "find k/rows of the set" and for highlighting "one group of cols".

labelEachGroup.description: Tag every group with its share of the whole ("1/rows") beneath it — the fraction-of-a-set labelling. Selected groups' tags go amber. Default false.

reveal.description: How many groups (rows) have their objects drawn; the rest show faint "ghost" outlines — a "to be filled" frame for the STAGED construct build (groups appear one at a time). The figure size never changes between stages (the empty frame is always there), so a staged build stays aligned. Default: all groups drawn. Clamped to rows.

occlude.description: Which derived readouts to hide as "?" — the question hook. A hidden value blanks in EVERY readout it appears in, so a visible readout never leaks the answer (anti-leak): "total" hides the product / addition / stem RESULT together; "rows" or "cols" hides that factor wherever it is shown (a missing-factor question — "cols" also blanks each addend and the division quotient, which equal cols); "fraction" hides k/rows; "ofAmount" hides the k × cols value; "division" hides the total ÷ rows quotient. The objects themselves always stay visible — counting them is the method.

highlight.description: Amber the result readouts (the product / fraction / of-amount answer line) for emphasis once revealed. Default false. Does not change which objects are selected.

show.description: Which derived readouts to render beneath the figure.

product.description: The product equation "rows × cols = total". Default true.

addition.description: The repeated-addition sentence "cols + cols + … = total" (cols added rows times) — the bridge from equal groups to multiplication. Capped at a sensible number of addends; long sums abbreviate with "…". Default false.

commute.description: Append the commuted product "= cols × rows" to the product line — the commutativity reading of the same array. Default false.

fraction.description: The fraction of the set "k/rows of the set" (k = select). Auto-on when select > 0; set false to suppress. No effect when select is 0.

ofAmount.description: The of-amount equation "k/rows of total = value" (value = k × cols). Auto-on when select > 0; set false to suppress.

division.description: The one-part division "total ÷ rows = cols" — the size of one equal group. Pairs with a fraction of a set. Default false.

factors.description: The factor / prime verdict: "total = rows × cols" for a rectangle, or "total is prime (only 1 × total)" when the array is a single 1-wide strip of a prime. Default false.

total.description: A plain total chip "total in all" / "= total" beneath the figure — for a "how many altogether?" answer space (pair with occlude: ["total"]). Default false.

stem.description: The fill-in stem sentence in a warm band: "rows groups of cols is total" ("rows rows of cols is total" in array layout). Occluded values show "?" so it stays leak-safe. Default false.

caption.description: A free line beneath the figure for words it can't compute, e.g. a short context note. Plain text, not derived. Never the question or an instruction: that wording is the block's text.

header.description: Optional short title centred above the figure; the top padding grows to clear it.

Occluded question — missing factor (? × 4 = 12), the row count hidden
Hard case — three quarters of 20: 4 ringed groups of 5, three selected, division and of-amount worked
